missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Nominative subject. 'Здоровье' is a neuter noun ending in -ье, here nominative as the subject of 'улучшилось'. 'Его' is the possessive and 'намного' intensifies the improvement.

Strategic focus: Accusative object. 'Здоровье' is the accusative direct object of 'укрепляет'; for this neuter noun the accusative matches the nominative. 'Человека' is genitive specifying whose health.
Strategic focus: Genitive under negation. 'Здоровья' is the genitive singular required after 'нет', meaning he has no strong health. 'Крепкого' agrees in the neuter genitive.
Strategic focus: Dative object. 'Здоровью' is the dative singular, the thing helped by 'помогают', which governs the dative. 'Пациентов' is genitive plural meaning the patients' health.
Strategic focus: Instrumental of means. 'Здоровьем' is the instrumental singular after 'расплатился', meaning he paid with his health. 'За успех' is accusative showing what it bought.
Strategic focus: Prepositional location. 'В здоровье' uses the prepositional 'здоровье' after 'в', meaning in matters of health. The dash links it to the predicate 'движение' in the nominative.
Strategic focus: Prepositional after 'о'. 'Здоровье' is prepositional after 'о', meaning caring about health. 'Детей' is genitive plural specifying the children's health.
Strategic focus: Accusative after 'за'. 'Здоровье' is accusative after 'за' in the classic toast; the neuter accusative matches the nominative. 'Ваше' is the agreeing neuter possessive.

Strategic focus: Nominative in comparison. 'Здоровье' is nominative as the subject being compared. 'Дороже' is the comparative and 'денег' is genitive plural, the standard idiom that health is worth more than money.

Strategic focus: Genitive after 'без'. 'Здоровья' is the genitive singular required by 'без', meaning without health. Note this abstract noun has no natural plural and is practised through varied case contexts instead.
